title: Compliance Codex: DriftWatch policy-as-code enforcement and automated remediation playbook
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Implement a policy-as-code system (Compliance Codex) that continuously lints deployed residency and retention configurations, surfaces evidence automatically, and offers safe automated remediation actions (DriftWatch) for Private and Dedicated deployments. This ticket covers design, initial implementation of the linting engine, drift detection signals, remediation playbook engine, and integration hooks for audit evidence export. Motivation: customers and auditors require provable, automated enforcement of data residency and retention rules across VPC and dedicated stacks; manual config reviews are a scaling risk. Scope: - Rule grammar for residency and retention (region pins, storage class, retention TTLs, auto-delete flags) - Agents to collect config snapshots and diffs from control plane and node-level configs - Drift scoring and heuristic rules to reduce false positives - Policy-as-code evaluation + policy registry UI surface (console) - Safe automated remediations with human-in-the-loop approvals for high-risk changes - Evidence packaging (signed artifact with before/after diff, timeline, actor) - Telemetry and SLOs for detection latency and remediation success Acceptance criteria: - A policy DSL defined and accepted by Security/Compliance - Drift detector runs against private deployments and surfaces actionable findings in the console and via webhooks within 5 minutes of drift occurrence in 90% of simulated events - Remediation engine can execute a reversible remediation for at least 3 policy classes (residency pin, retention TTL, encryption KMS) with audit evidence generated and stored in the evidence bucket - Playbook provides manual 'propose and approve' and automatic 'safe patch' modes with clear escalation rules - Integration tests and e2e harness covering snapshot -> drift -> remediation -> evidence export - Security review completed and signed off by Security team
acceptance_criteria: 1) DSL spec merged to docs; 2) Linting agent deployed to staging and detects injected drift events within 5 minutes; 3) Console displays findings with remediation suggestions and evidence link; 4) Safe auto-remediation can be enabled/disabled per-customer and has a rollback path; 5) Evidence artifacts include signed diff, RFC3339 timestamps, and the operator identity; 6) Security review completed
proposed_solution: Design a small policy DSL (YAML-first) that compiles to an intermediate JSON representation evaluated by an existing rules engine (we'll reuse parts of the policy engine from ENG-13821). Implement lightweight snapshot collectors (kubeconfig, control-plane config dump, SSM for on-prem) that publish to an internal Kafka topic. Build a DriftWatch processor that consumes snapshots, computes deterministic diffs, scores them, and emits findings to the console + webhooks. The remediation playbook engine will orchestrate idempotent steps via our runbook runner; each step emits a signed artifact to the evidence store. For safety, remediations require positive approvals for 'high' score findings; 'low' score findings can be auto-patched if customer opt-in. Use feature flags to gate automatic remediation per account. Trade-offs: - Using our existing engine accelerates delivery but constrains DSL expressivity; long-term we may replace with WASM-based evaluator. - Adding aggressive auto-remediation reduces time-to-fix but introduces potential for incorrect changes; mitigated via canaries and staged rollouts. - Collecting node-level state increases fidelity but adds agent maintenance surface area.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): DSL spec and linting agent; simulate 100 synthetic drift cases and verify detection latency. Phase 2 (internal beta): enable detection for 'redwood-infra' org only and present findings in Console with manual propose/approve flow. Phase 3 (customer opt-in): offer automatic safe-remediation for retention TTL and KMS tagging; provide per-account feature flag and audit trail. Phase 4 (general availability): support region residency enforcement for Dedicated and Private, provide policy registry APIs for customer-managed policies.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: drift_events_total, drift_detection_latency_ms (p50/p95), remediations_executed_total, remediation_failures_total, evidence_archive_latency_ms. Alerts: P0 if remediation_failures_total > 3 in 1h for production accounts; P1 if drift_detection_latency_p95 > 10m for >5m window. Dashboards: per-customer drift heatmap and remediation success rate. Link to monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/Compliance/DriftWatch
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL compiler and rule evaluation. Integration tests: snapshot producer -> drift engine -> finding. e2e: deploy test cluster with seeded misconfigurations for residency and retention, validate detection and remediation. Chaos testing: inject delayed snapshots and conflicting remediation attempts to validate idempotency. Include fuzz tests for the DSL parser.
references: Incident postmortem related to config drift: https://redwood.example/incidents/2025-09-config-drift-p1
comments: 2025-11-05 — Avery Chen: Initial ticket created. Drafted DSL goals and high-level design. Assigned to Diego for implementation planning.

2025-11-06 — Diego Morales: Ran spike to evaluate existing policy engine throughput. Found evaluation latency ~12ms per rule on current test models; acceptable for realtime drift detection at expected traffic. Will prototype collector as a sidecar for Private deploys.

2025-11-07 — Priya Nandakumar (Security): Security review requested. Key question: how are evidence artifacts signed and how is key rotation handled? Suggested using KMS-backed signing keys per-org. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-11-09 — Diego Morales: Prototype pushed: snapshot collector publishes to topic 'drift-snapshots.v1'. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6821. Added proof-of-concept diff algorithm that ignores ephemeral fields (lastSeen, leaderElectionToken).

2025-11-10 — Elena Ruiz (Product): From a product perspective, customers want a 'simulation mode' that reports probable remediations without applying them. Add to rollout plan. Also requested a cost estimate for enabling node-level collectors for large fleets.
2025-11-11 — Diego Morales: Updated DSL draft to include 'confidence' and 'remediation_scope' fields. Implemented proof for retention TTL and residency pin rules. Running e2e harness tomorrow.

2025-11-12 — Samir Patel (QA): Found flaky test: evidence signing test fails when system clock skew > 5s; added a clock-sync precondition to test harness. QA recommends we include monotonic event IDs to tolerate small clock drift.
